entry.title: security: close rebind and key-leak holes
entry.content:
security: close rebind and key-leak holes

Third-party audit, fixed 2026-09-17. The Host/Origin range checks now
match IP literals only, so 10.evil.com no longer passes, and a local
origin on another device is refused unless the request arrives behind
a reverse proxy it cannot forge. GET /api/settings no longer carries
the provider key; the key moves to write-only /api/ai/key and the
settings panel to a write-only flow. safeFetch re-resolves the target
twice to narrow the rebinding window. Responses gain nosniff,
no-referrer and a report-only CSP. JSON and aggregate upload bodies
are capped, and the socket request timeouts are bounded again.
security-gates.mjs pins all of it.

entry.title: brand: restore the real mark; lead image now shows activation functions
entry.content:
brand: restore the real mark; lead image now shows activation functions

The 0.70/250 book placement shipped in the last commit was a misreading:
the mark is one integrated drawing, not a small book floating on a ball.
At the export's own placement the planet's crown rises in the V between
the page tops, its gridded hemisphere hangs below the pages, and the
full-height spine runs crown to pole — which is the real logo, checked
against the designer's own SVG. The geometric culling stays: the pages
still cut the globe's middle band out by clip-path, not by paint.

The README lead image is retaken on the activation-function topic: the
previous chart was two mirror-image lines crossing — technically a weight
story, visually an X with nothing to read. The new one draws ReLU as a
blue kinked line and sigmoid as an orange S-curve, with the lesson text
reading both shapes, a numeric question, and the practice drill.

entry.title: brand: cull the planet behind the book; retake the README screenshot
entry.content:
brand: cull the planet behind the book; retake the README screenshot

The README wordmark rendered the whole mark with fill=none, so the globe's
grid showed straight through the book's pages. The book now clips the
sphere behind it (evenodd clipPath — SVG masks silently erase the group in
the rasteriser), and sits lower (0.70/250) so the mark reads as a planet
with a book on it. All brand SVGs and shipped PNGs re-rendered.

The README screenshot is retaken from a generated machine-learning course:
the old pie chart was a single green disc, because the Sun holds 99.8% of
the solar system's mass and left nothing for the other slices to say. The
new one shows a lesson on weights and biases with two weight settings
drawn as a rising blue and a falling orange line, and a numeric question
below.

entry.title: fix(docker): the image build needs tools/
entry.content:
fix(docker): the image build needs tools/

The image builds the frontend inside Docker, and vite.config.ts imports three files out of tools/ — which .dockerignore excluded as local tooling. The release run died with "Could not resolve ./tools/vite-plugin-sw.mjs", which reads as a broken dependency rather than a build-context problem, and it failed nowhere else: a checkout has the whole repo, so the suite, the desktop packages and every local build stayed green while the install path the README leads with was broken.

freshness-gates now derives the file set from vite.config.ts and follows each plugin's own imports, so a fourth one is covered the day it is added, and runs it against a matcher for the .dockerignore rules in use. Re-excluding tools/ fails three assertions.

entry.title: ci: fix attribution check on a first push
entry.content:
ci: fix attribution check on a first push

github.event.before is forty zeros the first time a branch is pushed, so the range was 0000..sha and git exited 128 — the check failed on the initial commit for a reason unrelated to its contents. Falls back to everything reachable from the new head, which also covers a force-push that rewrote the old before.
